title: A cooking order without recursion

tests.expect: [flour; water; salt; dough; tomatoes; sauce; pizza]

tests.expr: [string_of_int (List.length (topo (graph (List.init 40 (fun i -> ("x" ^ string_of_int (i + 1), ["x" ^ string_of_int i; "x" ^ string_of_int i])))) "x40"))]
let r = topo (graph (List.init 100000 (fun i -> (string_of_int i, [string_of_int (i + 1)])))) "0" in [string_of_int (List.length r); List.hd r; List.nth r 100000]

hints: Keep a stack of `(item, ready)` pairs as a list, starting with `[(root, false)]`, and loop while it isn't empty. Pop by taking the head.
When an item pops without its note: if you've started it already, skip it. Otherwise mark it, then push `(item, true)` and, on top of that, its parts with `false`, the first part at the very top.
When an item pops with its note, all its parts are written, so add it to the output. Build the output backwards with `::` and reverse it at the end.
explain: The stack holds the work a recursive walk would keep on the call stack. An item is marked when it is first expanded, so a shared part is expanded once, and it is written only when it pops again with its note, after all its parts: that is post-order. The parts are pushed with the first one on top, so they come out left to right. Nothing recurses, so the 100,000-deep chain is a loop of 200,000 steps.
